newsitem.title: CHINA: Ford says to launch China truck in December.
newsitem.headline: Ford says to launch China truck in December.

text.p: U.S. carmaker Ford Motor Co will start production of a line of commercial trucks in China this December, a senior company official said on Wednesday.

Ford and China's Jiangling Motors Corp , of which Ford has a 20 percent stake, would make about 20,000 of the Transit model vehicles in the first year of production, said Vaughn Koshkarian, president of Ford China.
"We are really enthusiastic about it in terms of starting production in December," Koshkarian said, adding he hoped output would rise to an annual 60,000 units within several years.

The Transit, which will be available first in a passenger bus version and later as a van and a chassis-cab, would be made from about 50 percent local parts, including a diesel engine built by Jiangling, Koshkarian said.
Ford would increase the localisation rate to 80-90 percent within two or three years, he said.
Ford was also considering boosting its stake in Jiangling to 30 percent by buying $54.5 million of foreign currency B shares the Chinese firm is to issue this month, he said.
Jiangling is already listed on China's southern Shenzhen stock exchange and said its net profit for 1996 soared 776 percent to 34.6 million yuan ($4.1 million).
The U.S. auto giant, which lost out to rival General Motors in bidding to set up a huge joint venture car plant in Shanghai, was also in talks to start making passenger cars, Koshkarian said.
"We are in discussions in China on cooperating for deals that we would hope will lead to passenger car production," he said but declined to give further details.
